method: Run each eval in a separate agent, 3 runs for each variant. Use the prompt in runner.md.
The variant 'baseline' uses the six source skills of Matt Pocock, called one by one by the human. The variant 'skill' uses plan-and-build.
The orchestrator plays the human. It replies only from the answer sheet in humans/<eval>.md. The agent never sees the sheet.
Score each run on its own. 'check' assertions: run score.py. 'judge' assertions: one grader agent for each run, with yes or no and one line of evidence for each assertion.

evals.name: todo-due-dates
evals.request: I want due dates on my to-do tasks, and a way to see what is overdue.

assertions.judge: The agent did not ask the human for a fact that is in the code or the README.
Each question to the human had a recommended answer.
The agent got the human's approval of a shared understanding before it wrote the spec.
The agent showed a prototype and asked if it is what the human wants, before it changed the production code.
After the prototype feedback, the spec or the tickets contain the change 'overdue tasks first, with OVERDUE'.
The tickets are vertical slices, and each ticket lists its blockers.
The final code does what the human asked: optional due date, YYYY-MM-DD, overdue means before today and not done, a command for overdue tasks, invalid date gives exit code 1, overdue first in list.
The final report is short and gives the test result.

evals.name: chores-rotation
evals.request: Rotate the chores fairly between the people in our house, week by week.

assertions.judge: The agent did not ask the human for a fact that is in the code, the README, or AGENTS.md.
Each question to the human had a recommended answer.
After the 'No' at the prototype, the agent went back to questions about absence before it changed the plan.

The agent made a questionnaire for Bram. After the human said that Bram knows, the agent did not ask the human for the answer to an absence question. A question about the process (send a follow-up, or use assumptions) is allowed.
The agent showed the second prototype and got a 'Yes' before it changed the production code.
The final code rotates weekly from Monday, shows this week and next week, skips a person who is away, and gives the chores to the person with the fewest chores (first in the list on a tie).
The logic stays in chores.js without DOM code.
The final report is short and gives the test result.

evals.name: todo-alias
evals.request: Let `ls` work as a short name for `list`.

assertions.judge: The agent kept the work small: at most 6 questions, one spec, at most 3 tickets.
The agent still asked for approval at the prototype or an equal small demo before it changed the code.
`python3 todo.py ls` gives the same output as `python3 todo.py list`, and the help text shows `ls`.
